editorial:
Imagine a creepy old estate where the owner suddenly falls into a deep coma and a hooded madman is on the loose from a nearby asylum. You get to follow Inspector Higgins and his partner Nelson as they try to piece together why this is happening just as the family tree is running out of heirs. It feels like a classic old-school mystery where you are trying to guess who the bad guy is while walking through dark hallways and dealing with weird family secrets. The vibe is very moody and mysterious, making you feel like you are right there in the middle of a puzzle.

What really works here is the chemistry between the investigators and the slow build of tension. While the pacing might feel a bit slow for some, the payoff is worth it because the twists actually make sense. If you enjoy stories where a detective has to outsmart a killer in a big house, you will love this.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that the hooded madman was actually a cover for a family member trying to steal the estate. After a tense chase through the house, Inspector Higgins figures out that the coma was caused by a slow-acting poison. The killer is caught just before they can get rid of the last heir. The movie wraps up with Sir Douglas waking up and the police cleaning up the mess at the manor.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic whodunnits and old English estates.
